system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK
GOVERNING RELATION: Thermal aging rate of transformer insulation follows the Arrhenius equation, where insulation life is exponentially dependent on temperature. The key magnitude is the top-oil temperature, which directly correlates with hot-spot temperature and thus insulation degradation rate.
USER CONSTRAINT: 30-day warning before next DGA sample
CALCULATED: Hot-spot temperature = top-oil temperature + 13°C (typical gradient for oil-filled transformers)
ASSUMPTION: Thermal aging rate doubles every 6°C increase in hot-spot temperature (Arrhenius rule of thumb)

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components:
- Existing sensors: top-oil temperature (RTD), load current (CT), ambient temperature (RTD), tank pressure (pressure transducer)
- Data acquisition system with 15-minute resolution (already present in modern SCADA systems)
- Analytics software for calculating hot-spot temperature and aging acceleration factor
- Alarm system with configurable thresholds
Procedure:
1. Calculate hot-spot temperature from top-oil temperature using the 13°C gradient
2. Calculate aging acceleration factor using Arrhenius equation with reference temperature at 98°C (typical for transformer insulation)
3. Track cumulative aging acceleration over time
4. Set threshold for alarm when aging acceleration exceeds baseline by predetermined factor

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY
Standard practice relies on quarterly DGA sampling, which provides limited visibility into developing faults. This implementation uses existing sensors with minimal additional hardware, only requiring software analytics. The maintenance burden is similar to existing SCADA monitoring, with the added benefit of continuous monitoring rather than quarterly snapshots. Cost class is software-only, making it significantly cheaper than adding new sensors or increasing DGA frequency.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Collect historical data from transformer with confirmed fault development (partial discharge or thermal fault)
2. Apply the aging acceleration factor calculation to the 15-minute sensor data
3. Determine the earliest point where the aging acceleration exceeds baseline by 2.0x
4. Verify this point is at least 30 days before the fault was confirmed by DGA
Instruments: Existing sensor data, historical DGA results, analytics software
Pass/fail threshold: The predictor must successfully flag all confirmed fault cases at least 30 days before DGA confirmation in at least 95% of historical cases
Duration: Test against 5+ years of historical data from at least 3 different transformers with confirmed faults
